newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF to decide on Magnetics buyer soon.
newsitem.headline: BASF to decide on Magnetics buyer soon.

text.p: German chemicals group BASF AG plans to reach a decision on which company will be allowed to buy its ailing tape unit BASF Magnetics GmbH before the middle of next month.

BASF chief financial officer Max Dietrich Kley told journalists late on Tuesday that a total of three foreign firms were currently interested in acquiring the tape unit and that a final decision on the sale would be reached by November 15.

Although BASF signed a letter of understanding with Turkish group RAKS Holding, promising them exclusive rights to the tape unit in late summer, BASF's supervisory board in September demanded that other potential buyers be considered.
The chemical giant's supervisory board had expressed concern that RAKS, postings sales of about 400 million marks, was too small and questioned its ability to run Magnetics.
BASF Magnetics, one of the world's best known tape brands, posted sales of 1.5 billion marks last year and employs 3,700 workers but has been posting losses for some time.
